memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Anyone who eats a sacred offering by mistake must make restitution
to the priest for the offering and add a fifth of the value to it'"
- Lev 22:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the two words: by mistake. God's law made careful provision for
people who did wrong without meaning to. There was a path forward:
restore what was taken, and add a fifth on top.

Two truths sit side by side here, and we need both.

First, honest mistakes are still taken seriously. Something real was
lost and had to be put right. Our culture often thinks that "I didn't
mean to" ends the conversation. Scripture says intention matters, but
so does restitution. Making things right is part of genuine repentance.
Zacchaeus understood this instinctively (Luke 19:8).

Second, and just as important, honest mistakes are not treated as
rebellion. There was no cutting off, no severe judgment - just a
practical way to restore.

Dear reader, some of us carry heavy guilt over things we never
intended. God is not looking to crush you. Where you can put something
right, do it humbly and quickly. Where you cannot, bring it to the
cross and leave it there.

Christ's blood covers our deliberate sins and our accidental ones
alike (Heb 9:14). Neither is bigger than His grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something I need to put right with someone, even though I
   never meant harm?
2. Am I carrying guilt God has already dealt with at the cross?
3. Does my repentance include practical restitution where possible?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, where I have caused harm without meaning to, give me humility to
make it right. And where I cannot, help me trust the sufficiency of
Christ's blood. Amen.
